card.summary: No fee, no key and no registration: Locationforecast and the other products of api.met.no answer any coordinate at up to 20 requests a second per application...

free_tier.stated: No fee, no key and no registration: Locationforecast and the other products of api.met.no answer any coordinate at up to 20 requests a second per application (total, not per client); the caller sets a User-Agent that names the application and gives a contact.
free_tier.notes: Over 20 requests a second needs a special agreement; throttled clients get HTTP 429, a missing or generic User-Agent gets HTTP 403, and coordinates are cut to 4 decimals. Locationforecast is refreshed every hour inside the Nordic area and every 6 hours elsewhere. Bulk path: the THREDDS server serves model files (NetCDF over OPeNDAP) for the Nordic and Arctic regions only, with no global files; historical observations come from the separate Frost API (see data-apis/met-norway-frost).

retention.stated: not applicable: the API serves current forecasts only; model archives are on THREDDS

egress.terms: not applicable: JSON answers; gzip compression is supported

record.interface_detail: REST over HTTPS GET at api.met.no/weatherapi (GeoJSON forecasts; also radar, nowcast, ocean, sunrise and others); gridded model files over OPeNDAP and NetCDF from thredds.met.no (an interface term for OPeNDAP is missing)
record.tooling: any HTTP client that sets a User-Agent; third-party client libraries are listed in the docs; THREDDS files are read with OPeNDAP clients, FIMEX or ncdump
record.chaining: A keyless global point-forecast source for 9 days ahead with a high per-application ceiling; history comes from THREDDS archives and the Frost API, not from this endpoint.

limits.value: 20 requests a second per application, total and not per client; over it requests are throttled with HTTP 429
coordinates to at most 4 decimals; 5 or more answer HTTP 403 on new products

record.binding_note: The 20 requests a second ceiling is shared by all users of one application; the User-Agent requirement is met by one header.

identity_cost.detail: No sign-up and no key: the institute's capacity-building page says the service is open to anyone with no registration; only a User-Agent with an application name and a contact address, website or repository link is required. A call with no key answered HTTP 200.

record.reliability_note: No SLA; a missing or generic User-Agent answers HTTP 403 and traffic over the limit is throttled with HTTP 429 or blocked.
record.confidence_note: Limits and identification rules are read from first-party pages; a keyless forecast call and an anonymous OPeNDAP call answered HTTP 200; the 20-requests-a-second ceiling was not driven. The docs link to thredds.met.no/thredds/metno.html, which answered HTTP 404.

card.summary: Free access to MET Norway's archive of historical weather and climate observations (quality controlled daily, monthly and yearly measurements of temperature,...

free_tier.stated: Free access to MET Norway's archive of historical weather and climate observations (quality controlled daily, monthly and yearly measurements of temperature, precipitation and wind, and station metadata) with a client ID issued for an email address; no numeric request quota is published.
free_tier.notes: Heavy traffic is defined as more than 1 request a second on average, which should be cached locally; users with high load or bad traffic patterns can be blocked. Large requests time out and are split by station or by time range. Bulk path: none beyond split requests; gridded model data are on THREDDS (see data-apis/met-norway).

per_object_cap.stated: requests that are too large time out; the vendor advises splitting, for example 1000 stations into 10 requests of 100

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a request

record.interface_detail: REST over HTTPS at frost.met.no with Basic authentication (client ID as user name, empty password) or OAuth2; JSON-LD answers
record.tooling: any HTTP client; examples for curl, Python and Java are published
record.chaining: The historical-observation companion to the keyless api.met.no forecasts: station data by source, reference time and element.

limits.value: more than 1 request a second on average is heavy traffic that should be cached; no hard number is published
requests that are too large answer a timeout and must be split

identity_cost.detail: A client ID and secret are issued after registering with an email address; each client ID must be tied to a valid email address. The form's other fields were not readable.

record.reliability_note: No delivery guarantee; clients with high load or bad traffic patterns can be blocked.
record.confidence_note: Identity and traffic rules are read from first-party pages; a call with no client ID answered HTTP 401, so a keyed call was not exercised.
